overview: The same DNA-protein material in two different states of packaging, seen at different points in the cell cycle.
genZNote: Chromatin is DNA in its comfy, spread-out house clothes. Chromosome is DNA dressed up and ready to be seen.

aspects.label: Structural State
aspects.valueA: Loosely packed, thread-like network of DNA and histone proteins seen during interphase.
aspects.valueB: Highly condensed, compact rod-shaped structure visible during cell division.

aspects.label: Visibility Under Microscope
aspects.valueA: Not individually distinguishable under a light microscope.
aspects.valueB: Clearly visible as distinct structures under a light microscope during metaphase.

aspects.label: Functional Stage
aspects.valueA: The active form — genes are transcribed from chromatin.
aspects.valueB: The transport form — chromosomes move and segregate during division; transcription is largely paused.

aspects.label: Composition
aspects.valueA: DNA + histone proteins, organised as nucleosomes ('beads on a string').
aspects.valueB: The same DNA and histones, further coiled and supercoiled into a compact structure.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Chromatin and chromosome are the same material at different packaging levels, not two different substances.
overlay.memoryTrick: Chromatin = relaxed. Chromosome = condensed for the move (cell division).
overlay.commonMisconception: A chromosome is not 'made of chromatin plus something else' — condensation, not new material, is the only difference.
